findings.title: Do not treat identity lookup failures as permission-cache misses
findings.body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` uses `cache.ErrNotFound` for an actual permission-cache miss, but it also propagates failures from `GetUserIdentifiers` (for example, SQL errors, unknown-user errors, or a canceled context). This code treats every non-nil error as a cache miss and immediately calls `getIdentityPermissions`, which performs the identifier lookup again. Consequently every affected Check request issues two identity-store queries during an outage or when callers send unknown subjects; List has the same pattern at line 180. Only fall back when the error is `cache.ErrNotFound`, and return other errors directly.

findings.title: Bound the per-resource denial cache before caching arbitrary denied names
findings.body: A denial entry is created for every denied `(user, action, name, folder)` tuple. `Name` and `Folder` are request-controlled and are not validated or restricted here, so requests for unique nonexistent dashboard/folder names continuously create distinct entries. In the in-process setup this service is backed by an in-memory `LocalCache` (constructed in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go`), and unlike the existing permission cache this key's cardinality is not bounded by users and actions. A client can therefore grow process memory proportionally to the number of denied resource names within the cache lifetime. Use a bounded/evicting cache or avoid negative-caching arbitrary resource identifiers.

findings.title: The denial-cache test does not prove that the denial cache is consulted
findings.body: The test claims to put an allowing permission in `permCache` to prove that the denial entry takes precedence, but it stores `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`. `checkPermission` treats that map as a denial, so the expected false result would also occur if `permDenialCache` were ignored entirely. Store `true` for this scope (and ideally assert that the backing store is not called) so the test actually covers the negative-cache short circuit.
